subject: EdgeBurst websocket slow-drip and 502 spike — exec attention
messages:
From: Alan Wu <alan.wu@edgeburst.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rapid 502 spike + websocket slow-drip during demo window

Hi David,

We hit a problem during a live demo this morning: between ~09:06 and 09:22 PT the demo client saw a flurry of 502 gateway responses and the WebSocket stream started delivering tokens in a very 'slow-drip' pattern (very small chunks, long pauses). The UI froze and the presenter had to restart the session.

Symptoms we captured:
- 502 responses from the fronting gateway
- client observed token chunks arriving in bursts then stalling for several seconds
- retries from the UI caused more concurrent short-lived WS connections to spawn

Attaching a screenshot from the demo and a short log excerpt. This is a high-impact window for us (demo to three enterprise prospects). Can you advise ASAP on mitigation and whether this is a known degradation pattern?

Thanks,
Alan
Director, Product
EdgeBurst

Alan — thanks for surfacing this and sorry you ran into this during a demo. We've kicked off triage. Rishi and I are looking at edge and runtime traces right now.

Initial plan:
- Collect harvest logs from the edge tier
- Validate if autoscaler missed a spike due to short-lived connection churn
- Try a quick mitigation: reduce model size for EdgeBurst account and enable more aggressive prefix caching to reduce throughput pressure

I'll update you within the hour with actions we take. If you have a recording of the demo or the exact repro steps that would help.

-David
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 11:02:20 -0700
Subject: Re: Rapid 502 spike + websocket slow-drip during demo window

Quick triage notes:
- Error-rate: 502s spiked between 09:06 and 09:22 PT, primarily at the edge proxy layer.
- Observed behavior: rather than a clean stream drop, tokens were delivered in much smaller chunks with growing intervals — we are calling this 'chunk clumping' in our notes. Client keepalive timers eventually tripped.
- Correlation: the spike coincided with a short burst of concurrent connections from the demo environment (many rapid reconnects). Autoscaler did not scale fast enough because connections were short-lived but numerous, which resulted in increased queueing at the edge.

Attachments: harvest logs and a short trace for the window.
[Attachment: harvest_logs_20280624.zip (application/zip)]
[Attachment: trace-edgeburst-09_06.json (application/json)]

Mitigation recommended (short-term):
1) Force a smaller model variant for EdgeBurst to reduce per-token compute.
2) Enable aggressive prefix KV caching for their tenant to reduce token synthesis.
3) Apply transient rate-limits on handshake retries to avoid thundering reconnects.

If this is a strategic deal at risk we should bring in exec attention for credits/compensations and a joint customer war room.

-rishi
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Exec visibility: EdgeBurst demo outage risk / streaming WS slow-drip & 502 burst

Team,

EdgeBurst (strategic prospect; estimated ARR $1.2M) experienced a production-impacting incident during a high-stakes demo this morning. The customer reported both a surge of 502 responses and a degraded WebSocket token delivery pattern (small chunks with long pauses) that caused their UI to freeze.

Summary:
- Incident window: ~09:06-09:22 PT
- Observable symptoms: 502 gateway responses; token chunking with elevated inter-chunk latency leading to client keepalive timeouts
- Probable cause: edge proxy backlog + autoscaler hysteresis under heavy short-lived connection churn -> backpressure into serving runtime
- Immediate impact: demo failure; customer asked about credits and recovery plan

Asks:
1) Platform (Rishi): perform the short-term mitigations (temporary model downgrade, enable prefix caching, throttle handshake retries) and prepare an RCA.
2) Sales (Stephanie): pause renewal/PO pressure; offer a goodwill gesture (three months credits) subject to final RCA.
3) Exec (CEO/VP Sales): authorize a 2-hour joint war room for customer follow-up today and sign-off on preliminary credits if necessary.

I've attached the HubSpot deal link and opened INF-5721 in Jira for tracking. I'll coordinate a post-mortem and a customer-facing RCA.

-David
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
